articles.summary: With its epic scale, a star-studded cast and a story rooted in India's cultural consciousness, \"Ramayana\" is expected to open to bring Rs 75-100 crore on
articles.body: With its epic scale, a star-studded cast and a story rooted in India's cultural consciousness, "Ramayana" is expected to open to bring Rs 75-100 crore on its opening day across languages with experts projecting lifetime collections of Rs 1,000 crore to Rs 3,000 crore if it resonates with audiences.The grand cinematic adaptation of one of the most enduring epics in India will make its debut in theatres on Thursday. It stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Goddess Sita and Yash as Ravana.Prominent film exhibitor Vishek Chauhan said "Ramayana" cannot be judged by conventional film review standards because a section of the audience will approach it through devotion and reverence."You cannot call "Ramayana" a classic film like 'Dhurandhar', 'Border' or 'Baahubali', this is a different genre of filmmaking. This is about religion, it is faith-based cinema."It is about the biggest deity in this country, Lord Ram... a huge audience will watch it as a piece of faith. If that faith connects, then there's no stopping for this film. It is a review and critic-proof film (in that sense)," the exhibitor told PTI.Chauhan, who is the owner of Roopbani Cinema in Bihar's Purnia, cited the success of recent faith-centric films like "Hanuman Ansh", "Karuppu", and "Irumudi", to highlight how religious sentiment can lead to unusual theatrical turnout."If a Rs 2-crore film on Neem Karoli Baba can do Rs 300-350 crore in India, then you are talking about the greatest religious tale ever told in this country. If it connects with the Hindu devotee base, 'Ramayana' has the potential to do Rs 2,500 to 3,000 crore," he said.Veteran distributor and exhibitor Raj Bansal said "Ramayana" could surpass the box-office collections of "Dhurandhar" franchise, which reportedly stands at over Rs. 3,000 crore."'Ramayana' can become India's biggest cinematic film. Most importantly, Diwali is celebrated because of Lord Rama and here we're coming up with a film on him," Bansal, who is the director of the Entertainment Paradise, a multiplex in Jaipur, told PTI.Exhibitor Akshaye Rathi said the film has the potential to set new box-office benchmarks, given its cast, technical brilliance and its scale."'Ramayana' is a story that resonates with every Indian, we all have grown up listening to this story and have deep emotional connection to it... If the storytelling finds resonance, then it will break every glass ceiling and set a new benchmark," Rathi, who owns multiple cinema theatres across central and western Indian markets operating across Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, and Chhattisgarh, told PTI.Sameer Munshi, chief operating officer of Miraj Entertainment Ltd, believes the Rs 1,000 crore milestone is within the film's reach, and said it can open at Rs 75-80 crore nett or Rs 100 crore (gross) across languages in India."'Ramayana' is a story that belongs to every Indian household, and it has the potential to be one of the biggest theatrical successes in Indian cinema. We expect the opening weekend through Diwali to be on par with, or ahead of, the biggest openers we have seen. This is also a film that will keep growing over weeks as families and repeat audiences come in through the festive and holiday season," Munshi told PTI.Ashish Misra, head of commercialisation at Cinepolis India, said the chain had sold more than one lakh tickets for the film and planned over 1,600 shows on opening day.He cautioned against judging the film's prospects solely through its first-day collections as its release coincides with Dhanteras and Diwali celebrations."One thing to keep in mind is the calendar. Friday is Dhanteras, Saturday is Choti Diwali and Sunday is Diwali, so until Sunday we could see some impact on collections from the festival celebrations, with families at home for the puja or out with relatives, especially for the evening shows. Monday is when the week properly begins," Misra told PTI.According to Munshi, demand at Miraj cinemas is particularly strong in Delhi-NCR, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka, while Tier-2 markets are tracking ahead of expectations.The company plans to screen the film across 225 screens, with 960 shows a day, offering it in Hindi, Kannada, Telugu and Tamil."There is no blanket price hike, especially in the Southern states. Most screens are at regular festive rates, and in Tier-2 and Tier-3 towns we are keeping pricing family-friendly. We've also created special festive food and beverage offerings to make the outing memorable," Munshi said.Rathi pointed out that advance bookings were showing greater traction in premium formats such as IMAX and 3D."While IMAX tickets are priced at Rs 3,000 and above or a little less, the average ticket price is lower, it is starting from Rs. 200, which is reasonable price for a Diwali bonanza of this scale and ambition. Also, the pricing will be different in different cities," he said.The film's prospects in the southern markets, however, appear measured due to the release of regional films like Suriya's "Scene" and Nayanthara's "Mookuthi Amman 2".Chennai-based trade expert Ramesh Bala said the buzz for "Ramayana" is stronger in Karnataka, where Yash enjoys popularity, while Pallavi's presence could attract audiences in other southern states.He expects "Ramayana" to earn around Rs 30 to 40 crore from the South market, and said the film relies heavily on word of mouth."The curiosity is more about the two South films and there's moderate buzz in the South about 'Ramayana'. It is not like other Pan-Indian movies. Films like 'Pushpa 2', 'KGF 2', and 'RRR' etc are mass action entertainers, while 'Ramayana' is a mythological film, and it is difficult to match the buzz with these movies," Bala told PTI.Rakesh Gothwaman of Chennai's Vettri theatres said audiences in the South often decide whether to watch films from other industries based on the response they receive."Since, 'Ramayana' is releasing one day before the two South language films, we will release it in both Hindi and South languages and then from Friday, 'Ramayana' will have its own space, not as big as 'Scene' and 'Mookuthi Amman 2'," Gothwaman told PTI.The film's long-term box office trajectory will depend on whether it can draw devotees of Lord Ram into theaters or not, according to Chauhan."It has only two possible outcomes: hit or miss, there is no in between. Either it will take a huge start and tank or it will keep running till 'Avengers' comes," Chauhan added.The film features music by A R Rahman and Hans Zimmer, with visual effects by Oscar-winning company DNEG. It is directed by Nitesh Tiwari of "Dangal" and "Chhichhore" fame and produced by Namit Malhotra and Yash.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. Festival da cerveja e shows são opções de lazer no fim de semana em Feira e região — Foto: Lindeilson | Sercio Freitas/ Divulgação | Reprodução/ Instagram

A agenda cultural do g1 Feira de Santana reúne eventos de música e teatro que serão realizados até domingo (8), na região. As programações acontecem em diversos horários, locais e com diferentes valores de ingressos.

Abaixo, você vai encontrar as seguintes opções:

✍️ A cantora, compositora e instrumentista Bia Cunha , natural de Santo Amaro, no Recôncavo Baiano, apresenta “Identidades”, um espetáculo que percorre diferentes faces da música brasileira através de um repertório que une canções autorais e grandes clássicos. Entre as interpretações estão obras de Djavan, Gilberto Gil, Edson Gomes, Tim Maia, Rita Lee, além das autorais “Tinta” e “Sereno”.

📅 Quando: sexta-feira (6), às 18h30 📍 Onde: Centro Cultural Sesc - Rua Cabuçu ,160 - Centro, Feira de Santana 💲 Quanto: R$2,50 (meia) R$5 (inteira) 🎫 Ingressos: no sympla

Xanddy Harmonia e Solange Almeida no Bahia Beer Festival — Foto: Redes sociais

✍️ Capital baiana da cerveja, Alagoinhas recebe mais uma edição Bahia Beer Festival . O evento, que segue até o dia 8 de novembro, reúne competições internacionais de cerveja, congresso do setor e shows gratuitos de artistas como Xanddy Harmonia, Igor Kannário e Solange Almeida.

📅 Quando: até domingo (8), às 10h 📍 Onde: Praça Mário Laerte - Centro, Alagoinhas 💲 Quanto: gratuito

✍️ Chupando Halles é um cantor e compositor brasileiro de arrocha, natural de Feira de Santana. Em 2024, começou a gravar vídeos nas redes sociais imitando a voz e o estilo do cantor Silvanno Salles (o "Cantor Apaixonado"). O nome do projeto surgiu de forma descontraída porque ele estava com uma bala Halls no carro no dia em que iniciou a gravação do seu primeiro álbum.

📅 Quando : sábado (7), às 19h 📍 Onde: Céu de Estrelas - Rua Frei Áureliano Grotamares, 52 - Capuchinhos, Feira de Santana 💲 Quanto: R$25 🎫 Ingressos: no local

Banda Sem Mais Nem Menos — Foto: Redes Sociais

✍️ A Banda Sem Mais Nem Menos é um tradicional grupo baiano de samba e pagode, formado no bairro da Rua Nova, em Feira de Santana. Com mais de duas décadas de estrada, a banda é bastante conhecida na região por sua forte ligação com a comunidade local e por animar eventos tradicionais, como a Micareta de Feira.

📅 Quando: sábado (7), às 21h 📍 Onde: Armazém 75 - Avenida Maria Quitéria, 545 - Brasília, Feira de Santana 💲 Quanto: R$35 (camisas) 🎫 Ingressos: no local

Neste sábado, o distrito recebe a Grande Montaria com Seresta e terá como atrações Índio Fera, Danilo Almeida, Marinho e a Banda Sorriso de Amor.

📅 Quando: sábado (7), às 19h 📍 Onde: Povoado do Rio do Peixe, Jaguara - Feira de Santana 💲 Quanto: gratuito

articles.title: Pregnant ‘Secret Lives of Mormon Wives’ star Jen Affleck shockingly files for divorce from husband Zac
articles.summary: The reality star is currently pregnant with baby No. 4.
articles.body:
"The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives" star Jen Affleck has filed for divorce from her husband, Zac Affleck, after more than seven years of marriage.

The reality star, who's currently pregnant with their fourth child together, filed a petition for divorce Tuesday in Utah, according to court docs obtained by TMZ .

Jen also submitted a proposed parenting plan, the outlet reported.

Jen, 27, and Zac, 30, met on the Mormon dating app Mutual in 2018 and got married in 2019. They share three children together — Nora, 4, Lucas, 3, and Penelope, 1 — with another on the way.

The "Dancing With the Stars" alum announced her fourth pregnancy in June on Instagram , sharing pics of her showing off her baby bump. Her husband did not appear in the pictures.

Jen and Zac have been open about their marriage struggles on "SLOMW" since Season 1. Jen shared that the two went to therapy to resolve their issues, and that their relationship was strengthened.

Still, the tension continued during Season 5, when Zac was not supportive of Jen's ambitions, including her wanting to appear on "Sports Illustrated."

"Zac was taught growing up to not only be modest himself but for it to be an expectation for women around him," she said in a confessional, adding that it's "definitely been hard navigating [her] career goals" while also honoring Zac's "traditional values and traditional views."

"I feel like if he truly loved me unconditionally, he would want to support me and I don't even feel like there's a conversation of a compromise," she continued.

She also shared that he threatened to divorce her if she got an acting gig and played a character in a relationship with someone else.

"I feel like Zac is not taking these dreams and goals seriously," she noted. "I think he's afraid of losing me."

Jen is set to star in the Hulu reality series' upcoming spinoff, "The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County," following the family's move from Utah to Southern California.

articles.body: The Lettermen co-founder, Tony Butala, died Sunday, Nov. 1, at the age of 87. Tracy Clark, the band's media coordinator, confirmed his death to The Associated Press with a statement, saying, "We have lost an integral member of The Lettermen family." "It is with profound sadness that we announce the recent passing of Tony Butala, founding member of the international recording artists ‘The Lettermen,’ and recipient of a Star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame," the statement read. "Our most heartfelt thoughts and prayers are with his children, grandchildren, siblings, the love of his life, the entire Lettermen organization and all who knew and loved him." JOHN ANDERSON, COUNTRY MUSIC HALL OF FAMER, DEAD AT 71 A cause of death was not disclosed, and there will be no public viewing. Details about celebrations of life in both Wisconsin and California will be announced at a later date. He co-founded The Lettermen in the late 1950s with Jim Pike and Bob Engemann, and the group released its first hit, a rendition of Fred Astaire's "The Way You Look Tonight," in 1961, which earned the trio a Grammy nomination. The band recorded 20 hits that reached the Billboard Hot 100 chart and earned four Grammy Award nominations. He retired from performing with the band in 2019, the same year Pike died at the age of 82 from complications related to Parkinson's Disease. Engemann died in 2013. articles.title: Jamie Foxx welcomes his third child, and his first with girlfriend Alyce Huckstepp
articles.summary: Jamie Foxx and his girlfriend Alyce Huckstepp welcomed their first child together. The "Ray" Oscar winner is also a father to two adult daughters, ages 32 an...
articles.body:
Jamie Foxx, 58, and girlfriend Alyce Huckstepp, 31, have welcomed their first child.

People reports that Foxx is now a dad of three. The Times reached out to the actor's representatives for details including the birth date and gender of the child but did not hear back.

Foxx and Huckstepp — reportedly a onetime fitness instructor who keeps a relatively low public profile — first sparked relationship rumors in August 2022 when she was spotted supporting him at the world premiere of his Netflix film "Day Shift," though they did not hit the red carpet together.

A year later , they were spotted leaving a group date at Nobu Malibu. Their relationship reportedly occurred after Foxx suffered a brain bleed that led to a stroke while filming the action-comedy "Back in Action" alongside Cameron Diaz, a health detail he would later reveal in his 2024 comedy special "Jamie Foxx: What Had Happened Was …"

In the aftermath of Foxx's health complication, Huckstepp was "there for him," a supportive presence in the actor's life, People reported in 2024.

The two split briefly in January 2025, but they were photographed three months later, coincidentally leaving the same Nobu restaurant. The couple remained together and were seen by People spending time at Kiki on the River in Miami last Halloween.

News of the pregnancy was first reported by TMZ back in May, with the outlet sharing that the Australian model was already "several months along."

Foxx is already a seasoned father with two adult daughters, ages 32 and 18. He welcomed oldest daughter Corinne in 1994 with ex Connie Kline, then Anelise Bishop in 2008 with ex Kristin Grannis.

Foxx has never been married, sharing in his 2021 memoir, "Act Like You Got Some Sense: And Other Things My Daughters Taught Me," that he's never been convinced that marriage is a good idea for him.

"It never seemed like marriage was necessary to raise my children in a safe and loving atmosphere," Foxx wrote.

Alexandra Del Rosario contributed to this report.

This story originally appeared in Los Angeles Times .

articles.title: Nazriya clarifies why she missed Suriya's three films before agreeing to star in 'Scene'; says 'It's just joke'
articles.summary: After staying away from Tamil films for over a decade, Nazriya Nazim is making her return with Suriya's upcoming film 'Scene.' The actress is also teaming
articles.body: After staying away from Tamil films for over a decade, Nazriya Nazim is making her return with Suriya's upcoming film 'Scene.' The actress is also teaming up with the actor for the first time in her career. During the film's Kerala pre-release event, she addressed Suriya's earlier comment that she had turned down three opportunities to work with him before finally agreeing to 'Scene.' Nazriya clarified that there was no deliberate rejection and explained why those earlier projects did not work out.Nazriya says she did not reject Suriya's three film offers deliberatelyResponding to Suriya's remark, Nazriya said that the earlier opportunities did not materialise because of date issues and other confusion. "Suriya sir said that I rejected three of his films. It's just a joke. Actually, it was because of dates and some other confusion. How will I reject a Suriya sir film?" she said with a smile. The actress also expressed happiness about being part of director Jithu Madhavan's film. "I'm glad I'm the first heroine of a Jithu Madhavan film. I have done action in this film. It was like a holiday as all are Malayalees," she added. Her comments offered a lighter side to the story behind her casting.Nazriya reveals why she stayed away from Tamil films for 12 yearsThe actress also spoke about her long break from Tamil cinema and explained that she was waiting for the right story and character. "The story and character I was looking for didn't come to me in the last 12 years in Tamil. That's why I didn't do Tamil films for the last 12 years," she revealed. Her return with 'Scene' is special as it brings her together with Suriya for the first time. The film also marks an interesting collaboration between the actress and Jithu Madhavan, who is known for his Malayalam films. Her action sequences in the movie have also raised curiosity among fans.Suriya's 'Scene' gears up for November 6 Diwali theatrical releaseDirected by Jithu Madhavan, 'Scene' is described as a mystery entertainer with elements of comedy and madness. Suriya plays DSP Inbaraj, while Nazriya and Naslen appear in important roles. The supporting cast includes John Vijay and Anand Raj, among others.Vineeth Augustian handled the cinematography, while Ajmal Sabu took care of editing. The film is scheduled to arrive in theatres on November 6 for Diwali. articles.title: 'Eetha’ actor Shraddha Kapoor REACTS to online criticism: 'My friends, directors, and producers keep SCOLDING me for not checking my phone'‘
articles.summary: Shraddha Kapoor has opened up about her approach to criticism and social media trolling, making it clear that she has little interest in responding to
articles.body: Shraddha Kapoor has opened up about her approach to criticism and social media trolling, making it clear that she has little interest in responding to negative comments. The actress said she would rather concentrate on her career and take up more projects than spend time addressing online reactions. Her comments come amid criticism of her Marathi accent and dialogue delivery in the trailer of her upcoming film 'Eetha'.Shraddha Kapoor on dealing with criticismIn a recent Ask Me Anything session on Instagram, Shraddha Kapoor was asked how she handles criticism. Instead of offering a conventional response, the actress spoke about how difficult she finds it to keep up with messages and notifications on her phone.She said, “I actually don’t handle criticism. What’s there to handle in that? I can’t even handle my WhatsApp. I don’t even have a manager, nor am I affiliated with any agency. My friends, directors, and producers keep scolding me for not checking my phone."Work matters more than online reactionsShraddha further explained that professional opportunities remain her primary concern. Rather than getting caught up in social media discussions, she wants to focus on doing more work and exploring new projects.“I’m not interested in handling any criticism. All I want to do is work, and more and more work. That’s it."The actress has previously maintained a relatively lighthearted public approach to social media interactions. Her latest remarks reflect her preference for keeping her attention on her profession instead of allowing negative reactions to occupy her time.Why 'Eetha' has sparked debateThe discussion around criticism comes as Shraddha prepares for the release of 'Eetha'. The film's trailer has generated conversations about her portrayal of Vithabai Narayangaonkar, a celebrated Lavani and Tamasha performer from Maharashtra.Some viewers have questioned whether Shraddha's Marathi accent and pronunciation sound convincing in the promotional material. Others have raised concerns about her dialogue delivery and overall portrayal of the iconic artiste. Who is Vithabai Narayangaonkar?Vithabai Narayangaonkar was an influential name in Maharashtra's folk entertainment tradition. She earned recognition for her contribution to Lavani and Tamasha, two performance forms closely associated with the state's cultural identity.Playing a personality with such a significant legacy presents a particular challenge for an actor. Cast and release date of 'Eetha'Directed by Laxman Utekar, 'Eetha' features Shraddha Kapoor in the lead role of Vithabai Narayangaonkar. The film also stars Randeep Hooda and Mohammed Zeeshan Ayyub in important roles. articles.title: Batman's bike from The Dark Knight could auction for £900,000
articles.summary: The "Batpod" features in a chase scene with Christian Bale's Batman and Heath Ledger's Joker.
articles.body:
A motorcycle used in Sir Christopher Nolan's Oscar-winning 2008 Batman film The Dark Knight is expected to sell for up to £900,000 at auction.

The vehicle is among lots being sold by Hertfordshire-based Propstore online and at Bafta in London from 4 -6 December.

The "Batpod" was featured in a chase scene that included Christian Bale's Batman and Heath Ledger's Joker and it also appeared in the 2012 sequel The Dark Knight Rises.

The prop is predicted to sell for between £450,000 and £900,000.

The Dark Knight was filmed on location in Chicago and Hong Kong, while large indoor sets were built at the airship hangars in Cardington, Bedfordshire.

Bale's complete Batsuit from Batman Begins, the first film in the trilogy, is also for sale, with an estimate of between £125,000 and £250,000.

Items from Indiana Jones's costume in Temple of Doom, including the protagonist's fedora, are being sold at the same auction.

The items came from the collection of stuntman Vic Armstrong, who doubled for Harrison Ford in the first three Indiana Jones films, which were shot at Elstree Studios in Hertfordshire.

They join other items from Game Of Thrones, Superman III and Conan The Barbarian.

Stephen Lane, the founder and CEO of Propstore, described the Batman vehicle as an "extraordinary feat of filmmaking and engineering".

He added: "Bringing together Indiana Jones' fedora, shirt and bullwhip in the same catalog is particularly exciting.

"With the fedora and shirt coming directly from legendary stunt performer Vic Armstrong's personal collection, they also tell the story of the remarkable stunt work behind the adventure."

articles.title: Not gold, but golden: Brass has its own kind of bling this Dhanteras
articles.summary: As consumers look beyond precious metals, brass jewellery is finding fresh favour this festive season, offering a combination of affordability and
articles.body: As consumers look beyond precious metals, brass jewellery is finding fresh favour this festive season, offering a combination of affordability and distinctive design. From sculptural statement pieces to heritage-inspired motifs, designers are reimagining brass as more than just budget-friendly jewellery. Its versatility, craftsmanship and ability to complement both Indian and contemporary outfits are giving the metal renewed fashion appeal. While some see it as an accessible alternative to gold and silver, others believe brass has an aesthetic identity that stands independently of precious metals.A medium for creative expressionFor Parna Banerjee of Vedaa, brass is as much about creative freedom as affordability. Its structural strength allows designers to experiment with oversized accessories, bold silhouettes and sculptural forms without the cost constraints associated with precious metals. “Brass is no longer just an affordable alternative; it is becoming a powerful medium of artistic expression, where fashion, sculpture and individuality come together,” she says. Bappaditya Biswas of Byloom shares this emphasis on the metal's design potential, although he is quick to distinguish its appeal from its price point. “I make brass jewellery not because it is cheap, but because I like the matte shine and its earthy golden glow, which goes with the textures that I work with,” he says. Rather than following trends, Bappaditya designs according to his own sensibility, using quirky elements that work particularly well with the metal. For Aditi Chakraborty of Anki Bunki Aditi, too, brass can hold its own as a sophisticated fashion choice. Pearls, semi-precious stones and gemstones can add richness to its adaptable forms, while thoughtful craftsmanship can make it suitable for both traditional and contemporary designs. “Affordability should never be mistaken for a lack of sophistication,” she says, adding that luxury is not necessarily defined by the price of a metal, but by creativity, craftsmanship and design.Heritage with a modern vocabularyThe growing interest in brass is also being driven by consumers looking for jewellery that carries a story. Monalisha Manna of Earthaments draws from cultural influences for collections such as her Jamdani-inspired range and Indian Summer, which features motifs inspired by jasmine, amaltas and mangoes. “What's trending, I'd say, isn't a particular metal but a particular sensibility: narrative, motif-led design that carries a story,” she says. She believes younger buyers increasingly seek pieces that reflect their cultural roots while fitting into a global fashion vocabulary. Karima Dawoodani of Soulworks has also noticed a growing appreciation for symbolic jewellery, with motifs such as hamsas, Ganeshas, trishuls and lotuses featuring prominently in the brand's collections. The lotus is among its fastest-selling designs, while an entire collection is dedicated to trishul jewellery. Karima believes changing consumer perceptions, aided by technological advancements such as anti-tarnish treatments and improved gold plating, have helped brass move beyond its earlier association with imitation or junk jewellery. Interestingly, Soulworks' core audience is between 30 and 55 years, a demographic that would traditionally gravitate towards gold. The brand has recorded a repeat purchase rate of around 30%, suggesting that consumers are increasingly viewing brass as a long-term jewellery choice. “People are not looking at brass as a trend-driven, one-time purchase but as jewellery they can return to and wear for years,” she says. While Bappaditya cautions against comparing brass jewellery directly with gold and silver, particularly during Dhanteras, given that it has no resale value, he points out that its appeal lies in its distinct aesthetic rather than its ability to replace precious metals. He also draws a distinction between jewellery and kassa and pital utensils, which retain resale value.Beyond conventional accessorisingAnother significant shift is the growing demand for versatile jewellery that goes beyond conventional earrings and necklaces. Parna sees younger consumers gravitating towards distinctive pieces such as ear cuffs, statement earrings and experimental headgear, while Aditi believes brass can transition effortlessly between a traditional sari and contemporary outfits such as dresses, blazers and jeans. “Versatility is no longer a bonus; it's an expectation,” says Monalisha, pointing to the demand for jewellery that can move between occasions and different styles of dressing. At Soulworks, this shift has translated into an expansion into unconventional accessories. Having introduced hair buns and hair cages in 2023, the brand continues to see interest in hair sticks, combs and other hair ornaments, often featuring motifs such as dragonflies. Brooch pins are another strong category, while the brand is working on sunglasses accessories, including chains and decorative clip-ons. Karima believes jewellery is increasingly becoming a medium of personal storytelling, with consumers using accessories across their hair, bags, collars and sunglasses to communicate their individuality, aspirations and beliefs. Bappaditya, meanwhile, sees the lightness of brass as an advantage when experimenting with modern shapes and textures. For him, the metal's fashion appeal cannot be measured by its price or by rising precious metal rates. “Fashion statement doesn't come with a price tag,” he says.Brass styles to look out forStatement earrings: Oversized hoops, bold danglers and geometric designs.Dokra and tribal motifs: Traditional craftsmanship reinterpreted in contemporary forms.Haslis and chokers: Rigid neckpieces, minimalist chokers and layered chains.Fusion pieces: Brass combined with pearls, semi-precious stones, wood and ceramic.Statement cuffs: Hammered textures, irregular shapes and antique finishes.Experimental accessories: Ear cuffs, brooches, sculptural rings, hair accessories and statement buttons.We have recorded a repeat purchase rate of around 30%, which tells us that people are not looking at brass as a trend-driven, one-time purchase but as jewellery they can return to and wear for yearsI make brass jewellery not because it is cheap, but because I like the matte shine and its earthy golden glow, which goes with the textures that I work withAffordability should not be mistaken for a lack of sophistication. articles.title: The New Yorker destroza 'La bola negra': "No es un monumento, es un fracaso"
articles.standfirst: La popular revista critica la última película de Los Javis
articles.summary: La popular revista critica la última película de Los Javis
articles.body: El éxito de 'La bola negra', la última película de Javier Ambrossi y Javier Calvo, Los Javis, está recibiendo, mayoritariamente, elogios en todo el mundo. Pero un artículo de la popular revista semanal The New Yorker ha roto por completo esta dinámica. "Esta película no es un monumento; es un fracaso", afirma Justin Chang, crítico de cine de esta publicación. El autor profundiza en su contundente opinión sobre el largometraje y apenas deja títere con cabeza: "Es como si los directores, blandiendo un rígido esquema narrativo y temático, fueran incapaces de coordinar los personajes, los diálogos y la acción al servicio de sus propósitos generales". Los directores, según Chang, apuestan demasiado alto con la película. "Pretenden erigir un monumento cinematográfico para la posteridad; en cambio, han producido una película que insiste, de forma arrogante y agresiva, en su propia monumentalidad", reflexiona. The New Yorker repasa las distintas historias que se relatan en 'La bola negra' y no salva a ninguna de ellas: "Están lastradas por la misma extraña falta de sustancia. Los dramas de la represión y la liberación gay se entrelazan de maneras más reduccionistas que esclarecedoras". El crítico de cine se la revista semanal la define como una "epopeya exagerada y recargada". Justin Chang afirma que algunos momentos de la película exponen "la fragilidad de las pretensiones poéticas y estructurales de Ambrossi y Calvo". Pese a la severa crítica de The New Yorker, 'La bola negra', estrenada el pasado 25 de septiembre, ha sido enormemente aplaudida en todo el mundo. También en España. En nuestro país, la película de Los Javis se ha convertido en la más vista del año con 5,5 millones de entradas vendidas y ha firmado, hasta esta semana, un total de 37 millones de euros de recaudación. Actualmente, es el tercer mayor éxito de nuestro cine, sólo por detrás de 'Lo imposible' (42 millones) y 'Ocho apellidos vascos' (56 millones).

articles.title: Cambios en la TDT hoy en España: qué canales desaparecen, cómo resintonizar y dónde ver La Séptima
articles.standfirst: Este cambio acompañará la llegada de nuevas emisiones en ultra alta definición (UHD o 4K) y el estreno de una nueva cadena en abierto: La Séptima.
articles.summary: Este cambio acompañará la llegada de nuevas emisiones en ultra alta definición (UHD o 4K) y el estreno de una nueva cadena en abierto: La Séptima.
articles.body: La TDT se prepara para uno de sus mayores cambios de los últimos años. A partir de hoy 5 de noviembre, millones de espectadores tendrán que resintonizar su televisor para seguir viendo todos los canales después de la reorganización de frecuencias que acompañará la llegada de nuevas emisiones en ultra alta definición (UHD o 4K) y el estreno de una nueva cadena en abierto: La Séptima. Aunque no habrá un apagón televisivo ni dejarán de emitirse los canales habituales, sí será necesario realizar una nueva búsqueda para recuperar algunas señales que cambiarán de ubicación dentro de la parrilla. La recomendación es sencilla: resintonizar el televisor a partir de las 08:00 horas del 5 de noviembre. Antes de esa hora no servirá de nada, ya que la reorganización de frecuencias no estará completada. Para hacerlo solo hay que acceder al menú de configuración del televisor y seleccionar la opción de búsqueda automática de canales. El proceso dura apenas unos minutos, aunque en algunos casos será necesario volver a ordenar la lista de canales. Quienes no realicen este paso podrán seguir viendo gran parte de la programación, pero podrían dejar de encontrar algunos canales hasta completar la nueva sintonización. Los cambios afectarán especialmente a cinco cadenas: - Clan - DKISS - Atreseries - BeMad - Boing Eso no significa que desaparezcan de la TDT. Simplemente cambiarán de frecuencia y será necesario volver a buscarlas para recuperarlas. La gran novedad será la incorporación de La Séptima, un nuevo canal privado de ámbito estatal que emitirá en abierto y que se sumará a la oferta televisiva nacional. Además, RTVE, Atresmedia y Mediaset ampliarán su apuesta por las emisiones en 4K, ofreciendo una calidad de imagen superior, con más definición, detalle y nitidez. La respuesta es no, al menos para seguir viendo los canales habituales. Los televisores actuales seguirán recibiendo las emisiones en alta definición (HD) sin necesidad de cambiar de aparato. Sin embargo, quienes quieran disfrutar de los nuevos canales en UHD deberán comprobar que su televisor es compatible con el estándar DVB-T2, presente en la mayoría de modelos más recientes. Los clientes que vean la televisión a través de plataformas como Movistar Plus+, Orange TV o Vodafone TV no tendrán que realizar ningún proceso adicional, ya que son los propios operadores quienes gestionan las señales. No obstante, si también utilizan la antena convencional para acceder a los canales en abierto, sí deberán comprobar que la TDT ha quedado correctamente resintonizada. La cuenta atrás ya está en marcha. El 5 de noviembre será una fecha marcada en rojo para millones de espectadores que quieran seguir viendo toda la oferta televisiva sin sobresaltos y disfrutar de la nueva era de la TDT en 4K.

articles.title: An acclaimed biography of Alexander the Great wins the Baillie Gifford prize
articles.summary: An “immersive” biography of Alexander the Great won the prestigious Baillie Gifford Prize for nonfiction, in the latest sign of booming interest in ancient Greece.
articles.body: LONDON — An “immersive” biography of Alexander the Great won the prestigious Baillie Gifford Prize for nonfiction Wednesday, in the latest sign of booming interest in the world of ancient Greece. Edmund Richardson’s “Alexander: God, King, Man” was named winner of the 50,000 pound ($67,000) prize at a ceremony in London. British journalist Kirsty Lang, who chaired the judging panel, said the book is the first work of ancient history to win the prize and “reads like a novel.” “It’s very immersive. You really feel that you’re there on the battlefield, marching across Central Asia and Egypt with Alexander,” she said. “And it contains a lot of new research,” including Richardson’s translations of sources from 12 ancient languages. Richardson, a professor of classics at Durham University in England, spent a decade — “far too long, down far too many rabbit holes” — researching the life of Alexander, who inherited a debt-ridden Macedonian kingdom at 20, conquered territory stretching from Greece to India and died at 32. “No one called him Alexander the Great in his lifetime,” Richardson told The Associated Press. “No one thought he was going to conquer the world. He was his father’s slightly disappointing son, even when he took the throne. He was a tributary, not the main event. And then he starts to do all of these astonishing things.” Richardson said Alexander’s military expedition “transforms reality more profoundly than almost any other event in human history.” “It connects the world up in ways that it has never been connected before,” he said. “It results in this flood of knowledge and understanding and ideas and religious belief and science and astronomy and art, crossing from Babylon to Greece, from Greece to modern-day Afghanistan, from Egypt across to Italy.” The prize judges called the book “a love letter to the humanities and the work of historians and archaeologists,” at a time when those disciplines are under pressure from university funding cuts in the U.K. and elsewhere. Lang said the book should appeal to fans of Christopher Nolan’s epic movie version of “The Odyssey,” which has helped drive a surge of popular interest in the ancient Greek classics. “They knew how to tell great stories,” Lang said. “Life, death, love, relationships, tragedy. They speak to the most basic of human emotions and motivations.” Founded in 1999, the Baillie Gifford prize recognizes English-language books in current affairs, history, politics, science, sport, travel, biography, autobiography and the arts. It has been credited with bringing an eclectic slate of fact-based books to a wider audience. The winner was chosen from more than 350 entries and beat five other finalists, including American journalist Patrick Radden Keefe’s bestseller “London Falling,” the true story of a teenager who died after being caught up in the shadowy world of London’s superrich. The other finalists were Nicholas Boggs’ James Baldwin biography “Baldwin: A Love Story;” Matthew Sweet’s life of romance novelist Barbara Cartland, “The Great Dictator;” Anand Gopal’s Syrian saga “Days of Love and Rage;” and Andrea Wulf’s “The Traveler,” about the 18th-century naturalist and explorer George Forster. Last year’s winner was Australian writer Helen Garner for her collected diaries, “How to End a Story.”

articles.title: Paris Jackson demands $600M from father Michael Jackson's estate in legal war with longtime executor
articles.summary: Paris Jackson accused executor John Branca of financial retaliation after she challenged his handling of Michael Jackson's multibillion-dollar estate.
articles.body: Paris Jackson accused John Branca, the sole executor of her late father Michael Jackson's multibillion-dollar estate, of financially retaliating against her and her siblings after she challenged his handling of the King of Pop's fortune. Paris alleged in new court documents obtained by Fox News Digital, that she and her siblings experienced a multimillion-dollar reduction in payments while Branca maintained an "iron grip" over their inheritance. She asked a Los Angeles court to order a $600 million distribution from her late father's estate into the family trust after accusing Branca of mismanaging the funds. PARIS JACKSON SAYS DAD MICHAEL'S UNUSAL RULE HELPED PROTECT HER CHILDHOOD Branca has been the sole executor of Jackson's estate since 2009. The pop star died that year from acute propofol and sedative intoxication leading to cardiac arrest. Branca's alleged mismanagement of estate funds included non-contractual gifts to colleagues, aggressive litigation, public attacks and a multimillion-dollar reduction in payments to Jackson's children. "Without belaboring the point, when Paris began challenging the administration of the Estate last year through her objection to Executor Branca’s non-contractual gifts to his colleagues, her challenges were met with scorched earth litigation, public attacks, and a multimillion reduction in monies provided to her and her siblings by the Estate," her legal team wrote. "This course of conduct and administration should not continue." In a separate filing obtained by Fox News Digital, Paris accused Branca of using estate resources for personal travel on private jets, improperly charging personal expenses to the estate and concealing the spending from beneficiaries. She claimed Branca acknowledged taking multiple personal trips and reimbursed certain expenses only after she investigated them. Her attorneys characterized the conduct as "outright theft" and a breach of his fiduciary duties. "Where the travel is of a purely personal nature, or in service of Mr. Branca's other clients or business affairs, it constitutes outright theft," the court filing stated. Paris also accused Branca of using estate funds for personal gifts, questioned more than $604,000 in credit card charges and reimbursements, and challenged $9.4 million in executor compensation, $1.4 million in payments to his law firm and roughly $835,000 in public relations expenses. She further alleged that Branca mismanaged more than $440 million in estate cash while pursuing entertainment projects that benefited him financially, including the Michael Jackson biopic, which reportedly required tens of millions of dollars in reshoots and rewrites. Her legal team urged the court to reject Branca's financial accounting and order him to provide a more detailed breakdown of the estate's spending. "Once again, Ms. Jackson’s legal team raises the same hollow complaints and fails to acknowledge the unique structure of the Estate, which is operated as a dynamic business, with customary costs and expenses," a representative for the estate told Fox News Digital. "No rhetoric can hide the fact that the Executors have taken an Estate that was $500 million in debt when Michael died and turned it into the most successful Estate in history, producing $3 billion in revenue and the biggest biopic in movie history, with a box office exceeding $1 billion globally." As for the $600 million distribution, Paris argued that her father's estate plan entitled his children — Prince, Paris and Bigi — to trust income beginning at age 21 and portions of their inheritance beginning at age 30. She claimed the executor had never funded the trust, despite Michael Jackson's death more than 17 years earlier. "As each child reached certain ages, Executors were to increasingly provide for each child’s independence." Paris' filing cited more than $2.5 billion in gross estate earnings and approximately $850 million in cash or cash equivalents as of December 2024. She argued that the estate could distribute $600 million while retaining enough money to cover outstanding liabilities. "Ms. Jackson’s counsel is well aware that the Estate is prevented from fully funding the philanthropic giving and individual trusts for the beneficiaries until several legal hurdles have been removed, including in particular the ongoing IRS litigation where they sought $700 million in taxes and penalties from the Estate," a statement provided to Fox News Digital on behalf of Jackson's estate said. "The Estate was able to secure a ruling to significantly reduce that amount, but the matter has not been settled and could still change." LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS "Further, the claim that the executor has withheld or ‘cut' payments is a complete fabrication," the statement added. "In fact, more than $200 million has already been distributed for the benefit of Paris and the other beneficiaries. Michael Jackson’s will is clear. None of his children receive a distribution until they are in their 30s. The Estate looks forward to the time when all issues are resolved so that their trusts can be fully funded as Michael wanted." A court hearing on Paris' request to transfer $600 million into the family trust is scheduled for Dec. 4. Behind the glitz of Jackson’s larger-than-life world, Paris said her father enforced strict rules to protect his children’s sense of normalcy. The 28-year-old model recalled in an interview on "Call Her Daddy" that her father required his children to finish their homework and chores before enjoying weekend activities, limited their television and movie viewing, and had them wear masks in public to shield their identities from the intense spotlight surrounding his fame. Paris said she understood that her father was famous. What she didn’t grasp was the sheer magnitude of his celebrity. "I just didn't know how famous ... There was definitely part of me that, like when I looked out my hotel window, and it was one of the times where, like, the alias didn't work and there's just like a sea of people with signs and stuff — I'm not so naive to think, yeah, everyone experiences this, you know?" articles.title: Magic And Muscles live-action movie makes a major reveal ahead of its 2027 release
articles.summary: A world where magic decides everything is about to meet a man who needs none of it.
articles.body: A world where magic decides everything is about to meet a man who needs none of it. Mash Burnedead has built his reputation on one simple belief: muscles can solve problems that magic cannot. Now, the unusual hero is heading to the big screen, with Mackenyu Maeda taking on the challenge of bringing him to life. The first teaser for the live-action Mashle: Magic and Muscles movie has revealed the actor's transformation, and there is a surprising detail behind his casting. Mackenyu says he spent three years building a physique worthy of the iconic character.Mackenyu Maeda prepares for Mashle with a three-year physical transformationThe biggest challenge of adapting Mashle: Magic and Muscles for live action is not simply recreating its magical world. It is finding an actor who can convincingly portray a character whose greatest weapon is his extraordinary physical strength. Mackenyu Maeda appears ready to take on that responsibility.The official website for the upcoming Japanese film released its first super teaser trailer and promotional visual on November 5. The reveal confirmed Mackenyu as Mash Burnedead, the central character of Hajime Komoto's popular manga. The film will arrive in Japanese theatres on March 19, 2027.Mackenyu is no stranger to bringing manga characters into live-action productions. His previous credits include Arata Wataya in the Chihayafuru films, Scar in the Fullmetal Alchemist adaptations and Seiya in Knights of the Zodiac. However, Mash presents a different kind of physical challenge.The actor revealed that his preparation began long before cameras started rolling. He also explained how much the character and the original series meant to him."Having thoroughly enjoyed MASHLE: MAGIC AND MUSCLES myself, I went into filming with the desire to bring that same level of entertainment to the live-action adaptation," said Maeda. "As the maximum preparation I could do, I spent three years from the day I received the offer developing a convincing physique that fans would approve of. I really hope you will check out the results on the big screen in theaters."That commitment could become one of the film's biggest talking points. Mash is not a typical fantasy protagonist who relies on spells, enchanted weapons or hidden magical abilities. His physical strength is the foundation of his identity. Mackenyu's preparation suggests that the production wants to preserve that defining quality rather than depend entirely on visual effects.Mashle live-action movie brings Yuichi Fukuda on board as directorMackenyu's casting is not the only important announcement surrounding the adaptation. Yuichi Fukuda will direct the film, bringing experience from several Japanese live-action adaptations of popular manga and anime properties.Fukuda previously directed the live-action Gintama films released in 2017 and 2018. His other projects include The Disastrous Life of Saiki K., Wotakoi: Love Is Hard for Otaku, Saint Young Men and UNDER NINJA. His experience with comedy-driven stories could prove useful for a franchise that combines exaggerated action, absurd humour and fantasy.The director also expressed excitement about the production and its cast."Starting with Macken, I was able to approach this film with what I consider to be the best possible cast currently imaginable. It was my first time working with almost all of the cast members, making every day a fresh and amazingly fun shoot! I really can't wait for it to be released."Warner Bros. and Fuji TV are overseeing the project, while CREDEUS is handling production. TOHO will distribute the movie in Japan.The timing also gives the franchise another major moment. The original manga ran in Weekly Shonen Jump from January 2020 to July 2023, concluding with 18 volumes. Its anime adaptation has already delivered two seasons, with the third season, The Tri-Magicathlon Divine Visionary Final Exam Arc, scheduled to premiere in January 2027.With the anime returning just months before the movie reaches theatres, Mashle is preparing for a busy year. articles.title: Rohini Hattangady recalls Dharmendra asking her to wear more make-up as she looked too young to play his mother in 'Humse Na Takrana': 'I wondered how much white hair we would need'
articles.summary: Veteran actor Rohini Hattangady has often played a mother to top stars even though she was younger than them in real life.
articles.body: Veteran actor Rohini Hattangady has often played a mother to top stars even though she was younger than them in real life. In a recent chat, she recalled a funny moment from the sets of ‘Humse Na Takrana’, when Dharmendra reportedly felt she looked too young to play his mother and asked for more make-up.Rohini Hattangady on playing mother to superstarsRohini Hattangady played Amitabh Bachchan’s mother in ‘Agneepath’ and ‘Shahenshah’. She also appeared as Dharmendra’s mother in ‘Humse Na Takrana’. Talking about taking up such roles, she told India Today, “It never affected me because when I do a role, it’s a role for me. You are doing a character. Main sochti nahi hoon ki yeh bada hai, yeh chhota hai (I was never bothered if the part is that of an elder or younger woman). I’ll always act according to my character.”Rohini Hattangady's funny first meeting with Dharmendra in OotyRohini Hattangady said Amitabh Bachchan was comfortable with her casting, but her first meeting with Dharmendra was a little amusing. During the shoot in Ooty, she went to greet him on the first day. Soon after she sat down, her makeup artist came to her with an unexpected request.She recalled, “My make-up man came and started working extensively on me. I asked him what he was doing and why we were still not done. He sheepishly informed me that I was told to put on more make-up because Dharam ji was saying that I was looking young. I wondered how much make-up I would need and how much white hair we would need. And what am I supposed to do because I am young?” she recalled, laughing.About ‘Humse Na Takrana’The 1990 action drama was directed by Deepak Bahry. It starred Dharmendra, Jeetendra, Anita Raj and Amrish Puri in lead roles. Rohini, who was born in 1951, was only 39 at the time, while Dharmendra was 55.Rohini Hattangady’s careerRohini is best known for playing Kasturba Gandhi in Richard Attenborough’s ‘Gandhi’ (1982). The role won her the BAFTA Award for Best Actress in a Supporting Role, making her the first Indian actor to receive this honour in the category. She also bagged the National Film Award for Best Supporting Actress for ‘Party’ (1984).Over the years, she has been part of many well-received films, including ‘Arth’, ‘Agneepath’, ‘ChaalBaaz’, ‘Pukar’ and ‘Munna Bhai MBBS’.Latest projectRohini was recently seen in the Netflix film ‘Meethe Mein Kya Hai’, directed by Radhika Bansal. The story follows a young widower whose grief eases during a happy Diwali reunion until his sister’s sudden marriage creates chaos at home. articles.title: María José Gómez, experta en protocolo, sobre el error que casi todos cometemos con las aceitunas: “Nos tenemos que tapar”
articles.standfirst: Los consejos más importantes a la hora de estar en una mesa
articles.summary: Los consejos más importantes a la hora de estar en una mesa
articles.body: Cuando uno acude a un restaurante, pocas veces se percata de los posibles errores de protocolo que comete. Ya sea a la hora de usar un tenedor o cuchillo, beber de una copa o consumir algún producto concreto, nadie está exento de saltarse alguna de las muchas normas que, eso sí, son cruciales cuando se trata de un evento destacado y se está acompañado de ciertas personas. María José Gómez, experta en protocolo, ha dado algunos consejos en ‘La gastrónoma’, acerca del modo en que, por ejemplo, uno debe consumir un alimento tan habitual como son las aceitunas. Una norma con ellas es que si las cogemos con dos dedos, el hueso debe salir con esos mismos dedos. “Lo podemos hacer de una forma más elegante y otra menos: una es tapándonos la boca, cojo el hueso y lo saco con los dos dedos, tapo y lo llevo a la zona de los descartes, siempre tapando. Otra es usando el puño”, explica, rechazando el gesto de sacar el hueso delante de todos los comensales. Esto se debe hacer, además, con otros alimentos como el pescado y sus espinas. “Nos tenemos que tapar”, insiste. En su publicación, sin embargo, algunas personas optan por aconsejar directamente no pedir alimentos como aceitunas con hueso y así evitar ese tipo de incomodidades. La mayoría, eso sí, optan por elegir la segunda opción y usar el puño, ya que de esa manera se esconde en todo momento el hueso de la aceituna y nadie de tu alrededor puede ver cómo sale de la boca. En cualquier caso, ese tipo de consejos sobre protocolo no dejan de ser útiles cuando uno acude a un evento importante y va a estar acompañado de otras personalidades.

It’s the day families bring home something new, whether a coin, a utensil or just a broom, light the first diyas in the evening and welcome Goddess Lakshmi, Lord Kubera and Lord Dhanvantari, the god of health. Along with the shopping and the puja, there’s another lovely tradition: sending warm wishes to the people we love. articles.title: Meghan Markle Reportedly Floats Idea Of ‘Living Separate Lives’ From Prince Harry After Becoming ‘Deeply Unhappy’ In The UK
articles.summary: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle are facing another major disagreement over what their future should look like, with the Duchess […]
articles.body:
Prince Harry and Meghan Markle are facing another major disagreement over what their future should look like, with the Duchess of Sussex reportedly unwilling to make Britain their permanent home.

Just months after returning to the country with hopes of rebuilding family connections, the couple is said to have very different priorities.

While Prince Harry wants to use the move as an opportunity to repair his relationship with the Royal Family, Meghan Markle is keen to revive her Hollywood career and regain the independence she believes she lost.

Meghan Markle Longs To Return To The US After Failing To Secure Royal Acceptance

According to Heatworld Magazine , Meghan has become uncomfortable with life in Britain after the couple's return failed to bring the acceptance they had hoped for.

Their recent public appearances have attracted attention, but they have also faced criticism, leaving the Duchess questioning whether staying in the country is worth the personal and professional sacrifices.

An insider claimed Meghan feels disappointed by how things have unfolded, especially with their frosty relationship with the royal family .

"Meghan's deeply unhappy in the UK, and feels embarrassed about how things have turned out," the source told the publication . They added that she believes the family has faced further public scrutiny despite making an effort to reconnect with Britain and the royals.

"If the royals don't want them, Meghan wants to go back to America, pursue her Hollywood ambitions and build a life where she doesn't need their approval," the source shared. "She wants Harry to understand the difference between leaving the door open to his family and allowing their entire future to revolve around whether they eventually decide to let them back in."

The Duchess Reportedly Suggesting She And Harry Spend Some Time 'Living Separate Lives' As She Pursues Her Goals

The Duchess is said to be considering a return to California, where she hopes to focus on her entertainment career without having to seek approval from the royals.

According to the publication, the insider noted, "Meghan wants to build the career she believes she's capable of having – she doesn't see why she should sacrifice those opportunities."

They continued, "She's told Harry she wants them to compromise, rather than expect her to keep bending. If he wants to remain in Britain, Meghan's suggested they spend significant periods living separate lives in different countries – but she doesn't see that as meaning their marriage has to suffer."

The possibility of reprising her role as Rachel Zane in "Suits" could make that prospect of a US return even more appealing. She has reportedly received an offer worth £3.75 million [$5 million] for a potential reunion, giving her another reason to consider returning to acting.

The insider explained that Meghan sees the opportunity as a chance to rebuild her career, saying: "Meghan feels there might be a real opportunity to get back into it."

"She's wondering whether this could be her chance to reclaim her career and finally prove that she can succeed in Hollywood on her own terms," the insider added.

Prince Harry and Meghan were given a "telling" sign the royals are done with them.

Prince Harry's Hopes Of Reuniting With His Family Clash With The Duchess 's Future Plans

Harry, meanwhile, appears more invested in making their return to Britain work. His recent comments about wanting to restore family relationships have renewed attention on the possibility of reconciliation with his father and brother.

The Duke has made it clear that he does not want the rift to remain unresolved, even though the path forward remains uncertain.

The difference in their priorities has reportedly become a source of tension. "Harry wants to put down roots, while Meghan wants the freedom to move between two worlds," the source said. She believes he should be able to maintain contact with his relatives without requiring her to put her own ambitions on hold.

However, the source suggested Harry is struggling with the possibility of spending significant periods away from his wife.

"Harry's understandably devastated by Meghan's mindset and desperately wants her to give Britain a chance," the insider claimed. He is said to fear that living in separate countries for extended periods could put pressure on their marriage.

Despite the disagreement, Meghan does not view a temporary long-distance arrangement as a threat to their relationship. For Harry, however, finding a balance between his family ties and his marriage may prove difficult.

Prince Harry And Meghan Markle's Hollywood Ambitions Face A Setback

Although Meghan is keen to return to the entertainment industry, the couple's production ambitions have encountered several challenges.

Page Six reports that two of their Netflix film projects, "Meet Me at the Lake" and "The Wedding Date," remain in development, with no apparent progress since March.

An industry source cautioned that this does not necessarily mean the projects are in trouble, explaining that film adaptations can take considerable time to develop.

"This is all part of the process. There are a lot of steps," the insider said. Still, the lack of visible movement adds uncertainty to the couple's plans for building a successful production company.

The situation has also been complicated by the departure of Chantal Pysnik, Archewell Productions' longtime head of nonfiction.

She was among the company's earliest hires and oversaw the production of the couple's Netflix documentary "Harry & Meghan." Her exit follows earlier departures among senior staff and a reported reduction in the company's workforce.

However, the Sussexes are said to still retain the support of Netflix co-CEO Ted Sarandos, with a source telling the news outlet that "Ted is still 100 percent behind them." Nevertheless, the combination of stalled projects and staff changes raises questions about how quickly their Hollywood plans can move forward.

Prince William And Kate Middleton Have No Plans To Rush Into Reconciliation

While Harry hopes his return to Britain will help repair his relationship with Prince William, the Prince and Princess of Wales are said to be taking their time.

A source close to the couple told People that they are not prepared to make an immediate response to the Sussexes' relocation or turn the situation into a public discussion.

"They are watching this space. It's private — they don't feel the need to say anything or demonstrate anything outwardly," the source explained. The insider also suggested that rebuilding the brothers' relationship would require patience, adding that "there is a deep sense of betrayal."

There has been little indication of progress between William and Harry, despite the Duke's recent efforts to reconnect with other members of the family.

Harry previously told the BBC , "I would love reconciliation with my family. There's no point in continuing to fight anymore." However, his relationship with William remains particularly strained, with one source describing it as "so broken."

articles.body: Russell Brand has been found guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault in the U.K. He denied the charges and was acquitted of two additional rape charges and attempted indecent assault. He has been taken into custody and is due to be sentenced Monday, according to BBC. Brand, 51, was accused of three counts of rape, three counts of sexual assault and one count of attempted indecent assault involving six women between 1999 and 2009. RUSSELL BRAND ACCUSED OF RAPE, SEXUAL ABUSE OF 4 WOMEN; COMEDIAN DENIES ‘SERIOUS CRIMINAL ALLEGATIONS’ According to Sky News, Brand acknowledged that he had been "reckless" and used his fame to pursue sexual relationships, but insisted that the encounters were consensual. He also told the jury that consent was "fundamental, essential and necessary." Brand has denied forcing any of the women to engage in sexual activity against their will. Last week, Brand's wife, Laura Brand, took the stand as a defense witness, one day after the comedian and actor testified. During Laura's testimony, the mom of three — who first met her husband when she was 19, and he was 31 — opened up about the start of their relationship. LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS The pair began dating in 2006, but split the following year due to Brand’s difficulty with monogamy and her "inexperience." "When I met him, I was aware that he liked women, and I was aware toward the latter half of that year that he was engaging with other women," Laura told the court, per Sky News. "I was not interested in having a relationship with him if he was sleeping with other people. I was invested; we both had told each other we loved each other, but it was clear it was difficult for him to be monogamous." The couple rekindled their relationship in 2015 and married in 2017. They share three children. Laura described Brand as "caring and kind, a wonderful father to our children, and an amazing, attentive husband," adding that he has an "eye for detail I have never known before." Prosecutors alleged that Brand committed the offenses against six women over a 10-year period. The women have testified in court about alleged encounters at a hotel, a bar, a radio station, a workplace and Brand’s home. As police explained in a press release, detectives began investigating Brand after allegations were made public by U.K. media outlets Channel 4 and The Sunday Times in September 2023. The outlets launched a joint investigation into the allegations, resulting in a lengthy article on the Times' website, as well as an episode of Channel 4's documentary series, "Dispatches," called "Russell Brand: In Plain Sight." Both contained a number of anonymous complaints, with women accusing Brand of physical and emotional abuse and bullying, as well as some instances of sexual assault. According to Brand, the encounters occurred during a "time of promiscuity" but were "always consensual." articles.title: ‘ER’ creator’s estate can sue over ‘The Pitt’ similarities, appeals court rules
articles.summary: An appeals court ruled Wednesday that “ER” is similar enough to HBO’s “The Pitt” for Michael Crichton’s estate to continue its lawsuit against the Emmy Award-winning show.
articles.body: An appeals court ruled Wednesday that “ER” is similar enough to HBO’s “The Pitt” for Michael Crichton’s estate to continue its lawsuit against the Emmy Award-winning show. Sherri Crichton controls the estate of her husband, one of the creators of “ER” who died in 2008. She filed a lawsuit against Warner Bros. Television and the creators of “The Pitt” in August 2024, alleging the team behind the new hit TV series was creating an unauthorized reboot of her husband’s show. According to Wednesday’s filing, Crichton and Warner Bros. entered into an agreement in 1994 that the studio would not make any new material derivative of “ER” without his — or his estate’s — permission. In the initial lawsuit, Sherri Crichton said she could not reach an agreement with “The Pitt” showrunners to create a reboot of “ER,” which aired on NBC from 1994 to 2009 and earned nearly two dozen Emmy Awards. She alleged in the suit that Warner Bros. began developing the reboot in 2020 without her knowledge and that she didn’t learn of the plans until 2022. In 2022, she said she engaged in negotiations with the studio, but that the terms were revoked, halting those negotiations. In the lawsuit, she alleged they should also have halted production of “The Pitt.” Warner Bros. filed a motion to dismiss Sherri Crichton’s case in August 2025, citing California’s anti-SLAPP law, which aims to protect citizens from lawsuits that target free speech. A judge denied the motion, allowing the suit to move forward. The defendants — who also include star Noah Wyle, “The Pitt” executive producer John Wells and showrunner Scott Gemmill — then took it to a California appeals court, which again sided with Sherri Crichton on Wednesday. “There are clear and numerous similarities between ‘The Pitt’ and ‘ER’; where those similarities lie, on a ladder of abstraction protecting only the more specific expressions, is a matter of ‘degree,’” the three-judge panel wrote. “Making favorable inferences in Roadrunner’s favor, as we must, we find the details here suffice for a prima facie case.” Both “The Pitt” and “ER” follow the personal and professional lives of a close-knit group of fictionalized doctors and take place in an emergency room. Wyle, an Emmy Award winner, also stars in both series. Wyle, Wells and Gemmill were all involved in “ER” and now serve as part of the team behind “The Pitt.” The shows’ main difference, however, is that “ER” is set in Chicago, while “The Pitt” moved east to Pittsburgh. Sherri Crichton did not immediately answer a request for comment. Warner Bros., Wyle, Wells and Gemmill also did not immediately answer requests for comment. From the outset, it was rumored that “The Pitt” would be a remake of the beloved “ER.” But before it aired in January 2025, the show’s creators made it clear that the new hospital-based drama would take its own path. Its first two seasons have already racked up 11 Emmy Awards, including two best actor wins for Wyle. Wyle, who also executive produces the show, recently spoke about his team’s decision to pivot from the initial idea to reboot “ER.” “We were going to start down an ‘ER’ reboot road that didn’t come to pass, but we sort of set a table of expectation for a medical show from us that we were then allowed to really fast-track the development process through because of that vacuum that we’d created from the near-miss,” Wyle told Amy Poehler on the Oct. 27 episode of her podcast, “Good Hang.” He continued: “And so, this just happened so quickly that it seemed like there was a larger force behind it, and we just needed to stay on the surfboard and let it push us.” Poehler then asked whether anything from those early stages of production made it into what eventually became “The Pitt.” “Well, I’m sorry to say for all the ‘ER’ fans, but once we uncoupled ourselves from that IP, it suddenly liberated the storytelling,” Wyle said. “It wasn’t about, ‘Who do we see again and what have they been up to?’ It’s, ‘What are the issues of the day and what’s the most cogent way to put them across?’” he added. “So it, in a lot of ways, it kind of liberated the narrative for us and allowed us to reframe and kind of modernize it and not have to pay any homage to traveled road.”

articles.title: Carson Daly announced as co-anchor of Saturday TODAY
articles.summary: Good news for TODAY fans who can’t get enough of Carson Daly during the week: He is the new co-anchor of Saturday TODAY!
articles.body: Good news for TODAY fans who can’t get enough of Carson Daly during the week: He is the new co-anchor of Saturday TODAY! Carson announced on TODAY Nov. 5 that he will be permanently joining Saturday TODAY alongside Laura Jarrett on Saturdays, while also remaining part of TODAY’s regular weekday broadcasts. He had been stepping in as an interim co-anchor on Saturday TODAY with Laura since September. “I should just say, I’ve been very lucky to have a lot of TV gigs, but this one’s really special,” Carson said on TODAY after the announcement. “At my age and at my stage of my career, to have an opportunity to come in and sit next to Laura and to learn and to get better at my job to be the best broadcaster that I can, it’s not something I take lightly.” “Carson has been an integral part of the TODAY family for the past 13 years, and we are thrilled that our viewers get to spend one more day of the week with him,” Libby Leist, Executive Vice President of TODAY and Lifestyle, said in a statement. “Carson and Laura make a great team, and we can’t wait for this fresh new chapter of Saturday TODAY.” He will make his official debut alongside Laura Jarrett, feature anchor Joe Fryer and meteorologist Angie Lassman on Nov. 7. “We’re going to have a lot of fun on Saturday,” Carson said. “But most importantly, the best part about the gig, like here during the week — which I’ll still be here during the week — is getting to go to your place of employment with such high-quality human beings. We are a family, and the fact that I get to spend one more day in this building, six days a week, is an absolute honor.” “I want to say Carson, you know how much I love you, you’re like a brother to me,” Savannah Guthrie said on TODAY. “I always say to anyone who will listen that Carson is like salt and pepper on a meal. He makes everything taste better. He makes every segment he’s in pop. You bring so much love and light, and I am so happy.” The TODAY family shared a Guinness toast in honor of Carson’s new position and as a nod to his ancestral roots, which he traced in the show’s recent visit to Ireland. “Oh by the way, Saturday (TODAY) is now broadcasting from Ireland,” Carson joked on TODAY. “We’re going to have so much fun,” Laura said on TODAY. He slides into the Saturday chair as the replacement for Peter Alexander, who announced in March that he was departing TODAY’s Saturday edition and leaving NBC News after 22 years. He is now a host with MS NOW. Carson first began with TODAY in 2013 as the host of the Orange Room, the show’s digital and social media hub at the time, and became a regular presence on weekdays. He delivers all the latest pop culture and celebrity news every morning during PopStart. “I had to create my own little world here just to be a part of this historic show. We were the nexus point between the broadcast and the audience at home,” Carson said on TODAY Nov. 3 about his beginnings with the show. The longtime television personality also has hosted NBC’s hit talent show “The Voice” since 2011. Carson will not be hosting the celebrity-centric Season 31 of “The Voice,” set to debut in 2027, but clarified in an Instagram post that he is still hosting the show. Carson has been a regular TV presence for nearly three decades. He rose to national prominence hosting MTV’s “TRL” from 1998 until 2003 and also hosted the late-night show “Last Call” on NBC from 2002 until 2019. Carson is also a father of four children with his wife, Siri Daly: Jackson, 17; Etta, 14; London, 12; and Goldie, 6. Four of his children joined him on the red carpet in October for the Project Healthy Minds gala in New York City to support mental health, a cause he is passionate about.

articles.title: Dafne Keen, la actriz madrileña de ‘Logan’, confiesa que le ofrecieron cocaína con 11 años: así la protegía Hugh Jackman
articles.standfirst: La intérprete de X-23 recuerda su infancia en Hollywood en un pódcast
articles.summary: La intérprete de X-23 recuerda su infancia en Hollywood en un pódcast
articles.body: Dafne Keen tenía solo 11 años cuando rodó ‘Logan’, la película que la convirtió en una de las revelaciones de Hollywood. Ahora, con 21, la actriz madrileña ha contado la cara menos amable de crecer en la industria del cine: en las fiestas de fin de rodaje le ofrecían cocaína cuando todavía era una niña. Lo ha explicado en el pódcast ‘Inside of You’, presentado por el actor Michael Rosenbaum. Al hablar de su relación con el alcohol, Keen reconoció que nunca ha bebido tanto como para tener resaca, porque es muy controladora con eso, y lo atribuyó a lo que vio de pequeña. “Me ofrecían cocaína en las fiestas de fin de rodaje”, recordó. Cuando el presentador le preguntó qué edad tenía, la respuesta lo dejó sorprendido: 11, 12 o 13 años. La intérprete aseguró que, por suerte, siempre dijo que no, y que haber presenciado aquello de niña le quitó cualquier interés por las drogas. Keen no ha revelado quién le ofreció esas sustancias ni en qué producciones ocurrió. Muy distinta fue su experiencia en el rodaje de ‘Logan’, donde dio vida a Laura, también conocida como X-23, junto a Hugh Jackman. La actriz describió al intérprete de Lobezno como una auténtica figura paterna que la protegió durante toda la producción. Según contó, Jackman se aseguraba de que nadie abusara de sus horas de trabajo, de que se divirtiera en el set y de que no se enterara de las tensiones que pudiera haber entre bambalinas. Además, le daba buenos consejos y mucho refuerzo positivo. “Es el mejor padre de pantalla”, resumió Keen, que desde entonces ha seguido creciendo como actriz en títulos como la serie ‘La materia oscura’ o ‘Star Wars: The Acolyte’. La actriz volvió a meterse en la piel de X-23 en ‘Deadpool y Lobezno’ (2024), un regreso que los fans de la saga celebraron.

articles.summary: El musicólogo habla de ello en su libro ‘Rosalía. Un universo creador’
articles.body: Rosalía se ha convertido en una de las mujeres más influyentes del panorama musical, lo cual tiene varios porqués. De averiguarlos y explicarlos se ha encargado el musicólogo y compositor Daniel Gómez Sánchez, quien analiza en su libro ‘Rosalía. Un universo creador’ la trayectoria de la artista. El experto argumenta que su curiosidad intelectual constante constituye el núcleo de su obra. “Estamos ante un genio de la música del siglo XXI”, afirma, tras hacer una investigación originada a partir de su tesis doctoral en la Universidad Complutense de Madrid. En ella, examina su evolución técnica, su formación musical y su independencia creativa. El autor, que lleva casi una década estudiando la figura de la cantante, repasa hitos como sus inicios musicales, la lesión vocal que sufrió a los 16 años, la inspiración medieval de 'El mal querer' y su apuesta por la independencia artística frente a las multinacionales. “Abordar un proceso creativo es un gran reto y no es fácil de hacer”, confesaba en una entrevista con ‘Noticias Cuatro’. Sobre si la psicología de Rosalía influye en su proceso creativo, Daniel lo tiene claro. “En palabras de Rosalía, la identidad para ella es algo elástico y eso la resume muy bien. Rosalía es una persona que tiene mucha sed por aprender. Hace muchas preguntas. Se apuntaba a todas las extraescolares que había. El ansia de saber es la esencia de su forma de crear”, ha explicado. “Es una artista curiosa y en eterna búsqueda. De esta manera, el musicólogo subraya que detrás de su éxito hay una obsesión casi enfermiza por el trabajo y la perfección. “He llegado a la conclusión de que ella es muy auténtica”, sentenciaba, apuntando que la Rosalía artista y la persona “están muy a la par”.
